title: Deduplicate Orders Keeping the Latest Entry
description:
The raw orders table has duplicate rows for the same `(customer_id, order_date)` pair due to an ingestion bug. Keep only the row with the highest `id` (the latest ingested) and discard the rest.

**Table: raw_orders** — `id`, `customer_id`, `order_date`, `amount`

Output columns: `id`, `customer_id`, `order_date`, `amount`. Order by `id`.
solution_sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id, order_date ORDER BY id DESC) AS rn FROM raw_orders) SELECT id, customer_id, order_date, amount FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY id

test_cases.description: 10 raw rows with duplicates; after dedup keeping highest id per (customer_id, order_date): 6 unique orders remain

hints: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id, order_date ORDER BY id DESC) assigns rank 1 to the row with the highest id in each duplicate group.
Wrap in a CTE and filter WHERE rn = 1 to keep only the canonical row per group.
explanation: The CTE assigns ROW_NUMBER partitioned by the duplicate key (customer_id, order_date) ordered by id DESC so the latest row gets rn=1. Customer 101 has 2 rows for Jan 10: ids 1 and 2 — id=2 survives. Customer 103 has 3 rows for Jan 15: ids 4,5,6 — id=6 survives. Customer 105 has 2 rows: id=10 survives. Total after dedup: 6 rows.
